title: xiom lint
concept: `xiom lint` statically analyzes code for potential bugs, style issues, and performance problems — catching issues before they reach production.
why: The compiler catches syntax errors. Linters catch semantic issues: unused variables, complex functions, potential bugs. Linting is your first line of defense.
theory:
## Static Code Analysis

```sh
# Run the linter
xiom lint src/

# Show all warnings (including style)
xiom lint --pedantic src/

# Treat warnings as errors (CI mode)
xiom lint --deny-warnings src/

# Fix auto-fixable issues
xiom lint --fix src/
```

### Common Lint Rules

| Rule | What It Catches |
|------|----------------|
| `unused-variable` | Variables never read |
| `unused-import` | Imported but never used |
| `dead-code` | Functions never called |
| `complex-function` | Function cyclomatic complexity > 20 |
| `too-many-params` | Function has > 7 parameters |
| `missing-docs` | Public items without documentation |
| `unsafe-without-contract` | Unsafe blocks without safety contracts |
| `unwrap-used` | .unwrap() call (use match instead) |
| `clone-on-copy` | Calling .clone() on Copy type |
| `needless-borrow` | Unnecessary & reference |

### Lint Output

```
$ xiom lint src/
warning[unused-variable]: variable `temp` is never used
  → src/main.xi:12:9
  12 |   let temp = compute_value();
     |       ^^^^
  help: remove the variable or prefix with `_` to silence

warning[unwrap-used]: consider using `match`
  → src/user.xi:45:20
  45 |   let name = user.unwrap().name;
     |                    ^^^^^^
```

### Configuration

```toml
# xiomlint.toml
[lints]
unused-variable = "warn"
dead-code = "deny"      # Fail the build
complex-function = "allow"  # Disable this rule
```
syntax_ref:
xiom lint <dir>              # Run all lint checks
xiom lint --fix <dir>        # Auto-fix issues
xiom lint --deny-warnings    # Fail on warnings (CI)
tips: Run `xiom lint` in CI with `--deny-warnings` — no warnings in production code
Use `--fix` to automatically resolve common issues (unused imports, formatting)
Configure lint rules per project — a game engine has different lint needs than a web server
Treat lint warnings as bugs — fix them before they become runtime problems
common_mistakes: Ignoring lint warnings — they often point to real bugs
Disabling lint rules globally instead of for specific lines where the exception applies
Running lint without --deny-warnings in CI — warnings accumulate into unmaintainable code
